title: The big lookout
hook: look back down the hill: from salaam on day one to a whole juz' carried in the heart

segments.voice: Yesterday, what year one gave, its tadhkirah: five camps, five lines. Your line was a year of remembering.

Some trails end at a lookout: a wooden rail, a worn bench, a little sign naming the peaks. People who've been staring at their boots for hours stand there and go quiet. Below, you can see the town where you started, small enough to cover with your thumb. Ahead, a further range you didn't know was there. Stand here a minute. This is the last day of camp five, and the last day of year one.
screen: `A WOODEN RAIL, A WORN BENCH.` → `THE TOWN WHERE YOU STARTED.` → `A FURTHER RANGE AHEAD.`

segments.voice: Look back down the hill. Yesterday you gathered the year camp by camp. Up here, you don't need the list; only a few landmarks stand out. Way down at the bottom, one word: salaam, a greeting that is also a wish. Further up, a seven-verse prayer you learned a piece at a time, long before you heard it called the mother of the book. And near the top, a whole juz', thirty-seven surahs, walked backward from An-Nas to An-Naba', carried in the heart, or at least begun there. Notice something else from up here. The path never went straight. It switched back from words to stories, from stories to practice, from practice to the text, then further in. From below, each turn felt like a new subject. From here it looks like one road, circling the same few things: God named and remembered, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ walked beside, a book heard aloud. Now look ahead. Year two is the book, surah by surah: starting from the Opening and al-Baqarah and reading onward, a little each day, all the way to the edge of the juz' you already know. It's a big range. The method doesn't change. The Prophet said, as Bukhari records, that the deeds most loved by Allah are the ones done regularly, even if they're small. That's how this hill was climbed: one small day at a time, from salaam to here.
screen: `LOOK BACK DOWN THE HILL` · `A WHOLE JUZ', BEGUN IN THE HEART` · `ONE ROAD, MANY SWITCHBACKS` · `AHEAD: THE BOOK, SURAH BY SURAH`

segments.voice: Choose the verse that stayed with you most this year, the one you wrote down, a line of al-Fatiha, al-Kawthar, or bismillah itself, and say it once, aloud, slowly, the way you'd speak at the top of a hill. Then stop, rest, and let the whole year lie behind you like a view. If you pray, you can thank Allah in your own words.
Salaam. Peace — the path's very first word, from the same root as Islam and Muslim, seen again from the top of year one. Today's word.
Your line: from here you can see. Tomorrow, year two begins. Day three hundred thirty-one, and year one is yours.

howItsDone: Many Muslims keep a small daily portion of Qur'an reading and remembrance rather than occasional long sessions, following the teaching that the deeds most loved by Allah are the regular ones, even if small.
